metadata_scope: Public titles, URLs, source-byte pins and stated inspection limits only; no source text or source files redistributed.

sources.title: Romyar Sharifi, Eisenstein cocycles for imaginary quadratic fields, Oberwolfach Reports 20 (2023), pp.1565–1568
sources.scope_and_inspection: Original question at printed p.1567/PDF p.25; DOI 10.4171/OWR/2023/28.

sources.title: Lecouturier, Sharifi, Shih, Wang, Eisenstein cocycles for imaginary quadratic fields, author-hosted manuscript
sources.scope_and_inspection: 47-page retained manuscript, retrieved 2026-10-14; no explicit revision label. Do not call it arXiv v2 or assign a mathematical revision date from HTTP metadata. Final reviews directly inspected sections 3.4, 4.2.1–4.2.4, 4.3 and 5.2 for moved primitives, reduced-point avoidance, auxiliary removal and cusp restrictions.

sources.title: Lecouturier, Sharifi, Shih, Wang, Eisenstein cocycles for imaginary quadratic fields, arXiv:2504.19125v1
sources.scope_and_inspection: 46 pages, distinct bytes from S02; existing source results retain their coefficient/level/character restrictions.

sources.title: Sharifi and Venkatesh, Eisenstein cocycles in motivic cohomology
sources.scope_and_inspection: Relevant motivic, Gersten and theta sections inspected in prior reviews; general g=2 source coefficient ring inverts five. Final review checked equation (2.4) for the reciprocal tame sign and sections 6.3–6.4 for the smaller GL2(Z) invariance group of the corrected cycle.

sources.title: Hyman Bass, K2 des corps globaux, Séminaire Bourbaki, exposé 394 (1971), pp.233–255
sources.scope_and_inspection: Sections 4–7 and rendered pp.238,243 inspected; tame symbols, transfer and finite tame kernel. Local Tate_K2.pdf has identical Bass bytes and is not a distinct Tate source.

sources.title: Howard Garland, A finiteness theorem for K2 of a number field, Annals of Mathematics 94 (1971), pp.534–548
sources.scope_and_inspection: Publisher metadata checked in prior review; finiteness statement inspected via Bass, not a full reproof of Garland.

sources.title: Bass, Milnor, Serre, Solution of the congruence subgroup problem for SL_n (n>=3) and Sp_2n (n>=2), IHÉS 33 (1967)
sources.scope_and_inspection: Corollary 4.3(a), pp.95–96, cited for stable SK1 vanishing.

sources.title: Daniel Quillen, Higher algebraic K-theory: I, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 341 (1973)
sources.scope_and_inspection: Standard localization and dévissage input; original full proof not reread by prior reviewers.

sources.title: Frédéric Déglise, Notes on Milnor–Witt K-theory
sources.scope_and_inspection: Section 2.5.1, Milnor residue characterization; Matsumoto degree-two identification also inspected in Bass §5.

sources.title: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties
sources.scope_and_inspection: Sections 5–6, Corollary 6.6, symmetric integral line-bundle identity. Also cited author scan https://www.jmilne.org/math/articles/1986b.pdf .

sources.title: Vladimir Voevodsky, Triangulated categories of motives over a field
sources.scope_and_inspection: Proposition 2.1.4 and integral Chow-correspondence convention; public author-hosted URL, not a private Dropbox link.

sources.title: A. B. Goncharov, Euler complexes and geometry of modular varieties, arXiv:math/0510310v5
sources.scope_and_inspection: Corollary 2.6, Definition 2.8, Theorem 2.10, and polygonal-face sections; level-localized/rational scope retained.

sources.title: J. E. Cremona, Hyperbolic tessellations, modular symbols, and elliptic curves over complex quadratic fields, Compositio Mathematica 51 (1984), pp.275–324
sources.scope_and_inspection: Record located, direct PDF retrieval failed with HTTP 502 in earlier review. Full proof not used; invoked Euclidean-face information checked in Goncharov. Bibliographic title and pp.275–324 checked against the official record for this inventory. The record links an Addendum and errata, Compositio Mathematica 63 (1987), pp.271–272: https://numdam.org/item/CM_1987__63_2_271_0/ . Only its metadata was inspected; neither Cremona paper supplies an uninspected mathematical input.

sources.title: Charles Weibel, The K-book: An Introduction to Algebraic K-theory
sources.scope_and_inspection: V.(9.3.1), V.9.6 for equicharacteristic Gersten; chapter III.1.3.6, III.6.1.1, III.6.5 independently inspected at https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.III.pdf .

sources.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory
sources.scope_and_inspection: Theorem 8.31 and Example 8.34, Chebotarev input for auxiliary prime existence.

sources.title: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory
sources.scope_and_inspection: Standard ray-field conventions; module conclusions proved directly in authored integrality argument. Final arithmetic review also inspected V Section 1, especially Theorem 1.7, for the inverse-limit local-unit/ray-class sequence.

sources.title: Emmanuel Lecouturier and Jun Wang, Level compatibility in Sharifi’s conjecture, arXiv:2208.06921v1
sources.scope_and_inspection: Cyclotomic comparison only; not an imported Bianchi theorem. Retained PDF header identifies v1, 14 Aug 2022.

sources.title: Masataka Chida, On the equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture for CM elliptic curves, RIMS Kôkyûroku Bessatsu B4 (2007), pp.197–221
sources.scope_and_inspection: Section 8; complete retained PDF and relevant pages inspected in residue review. Robert normalization retains mu12.

sources.title: Masataka Chida, On the equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture for Hecke characters over imaginary quadratic fields
sources.scope_and_inspection: Section 5, pp.6–7; Robert lattice product and Kato comparison, with twelfth-root scope.

sources.title: François Brunault, On the K4 group of modular curves, arXiv:2009.07614v3
sources.scope_and_inspection: Relative lane reference, §§2–3; source coefficient ring Z[1/(6N)]; P18 accepted with corrected scalar universal-unit argument; no general CM divided-power claim.

sources.title: Fukaya, Kato, Sharifi, Modular symbols in Iwasawa theory, arXiv:1402.3850v2
sources.scope_and_inspection: Historical provenance/comparison only, §§4.2.14–4.2.15. Referenced erratum full text was not recovered and is not a mathematical input.

sources.title: SageMath reference manual, Hilbert class polynomial database
sources.scope_and_inspection: Supporting software/database documentation, not a scholarly proof. The local checker verifies reduction arithmetic but does not independently derive H_-23.

sources.title: Dustin Clausen, Akhil Mathew, Matthew Morrow, K-theory and topological cyclic homology of henselian pairs
sources.scope_and_inspection: Theorem 1.4 independently inspected in the author-hosted manuscript during the final residue review. The Rochester mirror initially cited in the proof timed out. Used to state the hypotheses of rigidity and explain why it does not supply the missing residue-continuity theorem.

sources.title: J. S. Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems, second edition
sources.scope_and_inspection: I Theorem 4.10(c), printed p.57, and I Theorem 5.1, printed p.67, inspected as public primary text during final arithmetic review. Used for full-group higher-cohomology vanishing and the global Euler characteristic with the stated S hypotheses.

sources.title: John Tate, Relations between K2 and Galois cohomology, Inventiones Mathematicae 36 (1976), pp.257–274
sources.scope_and_inspection: Publisher bibliographic record checked. The original full PDF was inaccessible. The exact odd-prime S-integer comparison attributed to Theorem 5.4 was verified through Banaszak–Popescu, S25. The earlier file mislabeled Tate contains Bass and is not evidence for this article.

sources.title: Grzegorz Banaszak and Cristian D. Popescu, On the Stickelberger splitting map in the K-theory of number fields, arXiv:1008.1000v1
sources.scope_and_inspection: Theorem 1.3, Section 6, pp.17–18, and equation (37), p.22, directly inspected as primary research text in final arithmetic review. They state the odd-prime K2 comparison, S-integer extension, and H2 identification used here; no conjectural higher-K comparison is imported.
